research:
Research in Qianyi Liu's own words:
Mapping landslide susceptibility: "Which terrain and environmental factors best explain where landslides occur? I use landslide inventories to model these relationships and spatial cross-validation to test whether they hold beyond the training area." Topics: Landslide susceptibility, Spatial cross-validation, PU learning, Terrain analysis, Explainable AI, GeoAI.
Flooding in coastal deltas: "I combine hydrodynamic models and remotely sensed observations to study tropical cyclone flooding. Explainable models help me identify which environmental conditions matter most across a delta." Topics: Flood susceptibility, Tropical cyclones, Hydrodynamic modeling, Remote sensing, Ensemble learning, SHAP.
Learning from sparse inventories: "Can unlabeled terrain data help map landslides in places with few recorded events? I test whether models trained on geospatial patches can transfer what they learn to a new area." Topics: Self-supervised learning, Contrastive learning, Masked reconstruction, ResNet-18, Few-shot learning, Transfer learning.

projects:
Explainable Machine Learning for Tropical Cyclone-Induced Flood Susceptibility (Published). This project integrates hydrodynamic modeling, remote sensing-derived predictors, and ensemble machine learning to assess tropical cyclone-induced flood susceptibility. It uses interpretable machine learning methods to identify key flood-driving factors and produce spatially explicit susceptibility maps. Methods: Hydrodynamic modeling, ensemble machine learning, SHAP, GAM, remote sensing, GIS, Python.
Spatially Robust Landslide Susceptibility Mapping (Under review). This project develops spatially robust landslide susceptibility models using landslide inventories, terrain and environmental conditioning factors, PU learning-based negative sampling, spatial cross-validation, and model interpretation methods. Methods: Landslide inventory analysis, PU learning, CatBoost, spatial cross-validation, SHAP, causal analysis, GIS.
Self-Supervised Learning for Small-Sample Landslide Susceptibility Mapping (Ongoing / Under preparation). This project investigates whether self-supervised representation learning can improve small-sample landslide susceptibility mapping. It uses dual-view geospatial patches, ResNet-style CNNs, masked reconstruction, contrastive learning, and few-shot fine-tuning for spatial transfer evaluation. Methods: PyTorch, ResNet-18, dual-view patches, masked reconstruction, contrastive learning, fine-tuning, few-shot learning.
